# Client communication

Message clients in the app, by text or by email, keep up with the Messages hub, and request documents and follow up until they arrive.

## Messaging a client from a case

Click "Message client" in the case header to open the messenger beside the case. Every message, whichever channel you pick, is saved in the case thread, and in-app messages are also saved to the case activity timeline.

1. Choose a channel: In-app, SMS or Email.
2. Type your message, or open "Message templates" and pick one to replace the draft.
3. Click Send Message. You can also Copy the text or Save Draft to finish later.

> **Tip:** If the attorney has a booking page set up, use "Share booking link" to let the client pick a consultation time.

## How each channel works

1. In-app: the message appears in the client’s portal and in the case thread.
2. SMS: the message is texted to the client’s mobile number and saved in the thread. You see a confirmation showing the number it went to.
3. Email: the message is saved in the thread and the client is emailed to let them know a message is waiting.

## When a text cannot be delivered

If a text cannot be sent, the message is still saved in the thread and you see a notice explaining that the text was not sent and why. Try Email instead, or, if the number on file is wrong, correct it using Edit in the case header.

## The Messages hub

Case Management → Messages brings all your conversations into one place, with unread counts on each tab.

1. Clients: client and adjuster threads across all your cases.
2. Team: your firm’s internal team chat.
3. Mentions: places where a teammate has @mentioned you.

> **Tip:** Staff see the Clients tab only if their role includes "Client communication". Team and Mentions are shown to attorneys.

Where in the app: **Open Messages** (`/attorney-dashboard/cases/messages`)

## Requesting documents

Ask the client for files from the case’s Documents tab. The client gets one link with everything you asked for.

1. Open the case, go to Documents and choose Request documents.
2. Pick the items you need. Use "Other…" to describe anything not on the list, such as a rideshare trip receipt.
3. Choose Email or Text as the delivery method and send the packet.

> **Tip:** Items that are already part of an open request are greyed out. Send a reminder for them instead of requesting them twice.

## Tracking requests and nudging

The Requests view on the Documents tab shows each requested item moving through Requested, Received and Reviewed. Items still with the client are listed under "Waiting on the client".

1. For an item still at Requested, click Nudge and choose text or email to send a reminder. The row then shows when the client was last reminded.
2. When files arrive, open them from the row and click "Mark reviewed" once you have checked them.

## Client notes on requests and evidence

Clients can leave a note on any document you request and on every evidence category in their portal, for example to explain that they did not see a doctor or that a report is on its way. Notes on a request appear as a "Client note" under that item in Requests. Notes on evidence categories are collected in a "Client notes on evidence" card on the case’s Documents tab, newest first.

> **Tip:** Read client notes before nudging. A note often explains why a document is missing, which saves an unnecessary reminder.
